summary.text: A 55-year-old woman with MSI-H metastatic endometrial adenocarcinoma had surgical resection and adjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin combined with tislelizumab 200 mg, followed by tislelizumab maintenance therapy. One week after the 22nd dose (February 2024) she developed a decline in bilateral visual acuity and presented to ophthalmology 1 month after symptom onset.

Baseline examination showed bilateral conjunctival hyperemia, keratic precipitates, anterior chamber cells and optic disc and retinal edema, with choroidal folds and subretinal fluid on OCT and a relative afferent pupillary defect in the left eye. The diagnosis was immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated uveitis resembling Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada syndrome, graded CTCAE grade 2.

After multidisciplinary consultation tislelizumab was withdrawn. She received transcutaneous periocular triamcinolone acetonide injections, the second of 40 mg after the 3-week visit, with topical corticosteroid and mydriatic or cycloplegic eye drops, and without systemic corticosteroids.

By 3 months best-corrected visual acuity was 0.00 logMAR in both eyes, anterior chamber cells and subretinal fluid had resolved, and ocular findings were stable at 1 year. No tumor progression was seen after ICI cessation.

summary.text: A 66-year-old man was diagnosed with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, stage IV with pleural metastasis, in June 2024 and started first-line etoposide-carboplatin with tislelizumab 200 mg. After his fifth cycle in September 2024 he developed bilateral visual decline and was referred for ophthalmic evaluation.

Baseline BCVA was 1.00 logMAR in both eyes with bilateral conjunctival hyperemia, numerous pigmented keratic precipitates, anterior chamber cells 4+, optic disc and retinal edema, and choroidal folds with subretinal fluid on OCT. He was diagnosed with immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated uveitis as Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada-like syndrome, CTCAE grade 4.

Tislelizumab was discontinued after multidisciplinary consultation. He received transcutaneous periocular triamcinolone acetonide 40 mg with topical corticosteroid and mydriatic eye drops, and later a second 40 mg injection with continued drops, without systemic corticosteroids.
By 3 months BCVA improved to 0.10 logMAR in both eyes and anterior chamber cells resolved completely, and ocular findings were stable at 6 months. No tumor progression was seen after ICI cessation.
